learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the fascinating properties of tangents to a circle and prove key theorems regarding their lengths and angles!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A secant is a line that cuts a circle at two distinct points. A tangent is a special line that touches the circle at exactly one point (the point of contact).
The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular (at 90 degrees) to the radius drawn through the point of contact.
The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are exactly equal. (This creates two congruent right-angled triangles).
A circle can have at most two parallel tangents, and they are located at opposite ends of a diameter.

fun_activity.title: 🚲 The Bicycle Wheel
fun_activity.instructions: Look at a bicycle on the ground. The road acts as a 'tangent' to the wheel. The spoke going straight down to where the tire touches the road is the 'radius'. Notice how they form a perfect 90-degree angle!

exam_tips: 📌 The proof for Theorem 10.2 (Lengths of tangents from an external point are equal) is highly important for the board exams.
📌 Pythagoras theorem is your best friend in this chapter. Because tangents form 90° angles with radii, you will constantly use a² + b² = c² to find missing lengths.
📌 Remember that the center of the circle lies on the bisector of the angle between the two tangents drawn from an external point.
quick_recap: ⭐ There is only ONE tangent at a point on the circle.
⭐ You cannot draw any tangent from a point INSIDE the circle.
⭐ The tangent is a special case of the secant when the two endpoints of its corresponding chord coincide.
